$comment: Runtime witness for shipped <time.h>'s 64-bit time_t path on EVERY hosted format, baseline AND the `release` shippedPipeline arm. WHY IT IS NOT A DUPLICATE of the pre-existing `shipped_time`: that example uses localtime_r, a POSIX name gated availableObjectFormats:[elf,macho], so it has NO pe arm and cannot witness the Windows path at all. Added by the pe CRT migration (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION Phase 2), which rebinds time.json msvcrt.dll -> ucrtbase.dll: UCRT does not export the bare names, so time/gmtime/mktime reach it through pe macros onto _time64/_gmtime64/_mktime64. That mapping is correct ONLY because time_t is declared 64-bit (i64 'long long' on LLP64); pointing those macros at the 32-bit entry points, or narrowing the typedef, would produce NO link error and NO diagnostic — just silently wrong dates. ★ THE DECISIVE ASSERTION is the year-2100 conversion: an epoch past 2^31 seconds cannot survive a 32-bit time_t (it wraps to ~1901), so a 32-bit regression fails here loudly and specifically, where a 'current time looks plausible' check would sail past it. All epochs are FIXED constants read through mutable globals — never the wall clock — so every assertion is exact and timezone-independent (gmtime is UTC by definition, so no local-time/DST variation can enter) and the release arm cannot const-fold the operands away. Only the nine struct-tm fields common to all three format variants are read; the elf/macho tm_gmtoff/tm_zone tail is deliberately untouched. Each check has its own exit code (60..90) so a regression names the exact field. exit = 42.
